sections.existing:
- [SEAL Whitehat Safe Harbor](https://frameworks.securityalliance.org/safe-harbor/whitehat/) lets a white hat step in only during an exploit under way or imminent, on a protocol that adopted it, for a bounty usually 10% capped at $1 million ([SEAL](https://securityalliance.org/safe-harbor)). A good start with a narrow use: a white hat may not act on a known hole before an attacker does.
- [DART](https://assetrecovery.io/) (Digital Asset Recovery Technologies) and the independent Crypto Recovery Trust it works with are the closest model: a Wyoming statutory trust with an independent trustee takes crypto from white hats, gives them legal cover and returns it to verified original owners where the law allows.
- About 70,500 ETH from TheDAO's 2016 refund contracts is still unclaimed a decade later ([thedao.fund](https://thedao.fund)): even a famous refund never reaches every owner.
- [Kleros](https://kleros.io/) arbitration, for disputed claims.

This RFP aims to go further than Safe Harbor: if a white hat can take exposed money, they should.
sections.hard_req:
1. Victims pay for their rescue with a haircut on the return or a fee to collect it. That funds an equal rescuer bounty and operator fee, paid only on returns to verified owners: An example payout scheme could be: 2% each of the first $10 million, 0.25% to $100 million, 0.06% to $1 billion and 0.01% above (about $200,000 each at $10 million, $425,000 at $100 million and $1 million at $1 billion). Tiers apply per case, and a case is one incident with all its related addresses, chains and staged returns. Rates may rise case by case, within a published ceiling and set before the case is accepted, when few owners are likely to come forward. The proposal shows how the fee sustains the service after the grant, even with few claims and zero yield.
2. Published rules for proving ownership, including for leaked or weak keys (a signature from the exposed key proves nothing on its own), and a dispute path to a neutral arbiter.
3. A licensed firm's legal opinion covers custody, money transmission, sanctions, unclaimed property, how far rescuers can be paid without KYC, and what protection rescuers get when they hand funds over. Every return and bounty is sanctions-screened.
4. Funds nobody claims become an endowment: once they count as lost or abandoned under applicable law or a rule the operator publishes before the rescue, the operator may stake them or earn other low-risk yield and keep that yield, but every claim stays open and the principal stays available to pay it for at least 7 years from the rescue.
5. Rescued funds, including any staked under Hard requirement 4, sit only in audited code, such as an unmodified Safe, or with an independent trustee or regulated custodian, kept apart per case and from the operator's own funds, and the operator can't move them alone.
6. A public case page lists every deposit, return and endowment balance, each valued in USD at its block by a published onchain query: Chainlink feed, else relevant DEX TWAP (e.g. Uniswap v3 TWAP); anything else counts as $0.
7. Rescuers may stay unnamed in public. Where the law requires identity checks for bounties, the proposal says which checks and why, and the legal opinion in Hard requirement 3 confirms them. Owners' identities and evidence stay with the operator; the technical reviewer inspects counted case files and keeps no copies.
8. Code is open source, under a license the bidder states.
9. A case counts only if the funds were rescued after the award starts and its case page links the onchain trail from exploited contract or leaked address to owner. The technical reviewer also confirms the owner had the funds before the incident, no protocol could have recovered the funds itself, the owner is not the operator, its staff or an affiliate, the exposed contract or key was not deployed or funded by the rescuer, the operator or their affiliates, counted rescuers are not each other's staff or affiliates, and in each adoption milestone at most one counted rescuer is the operator or tied to it. Milestones count what owners receive, after bounty, fee and gas.
10. The operating legal entity signs an indemnification agreement with every white hat who hands it funds, so if a white hat is sued over a good-faith rescue handed to the service, the entity covers their legal defense.
sections.in_scope:
Legal setup (a new entity or an existing one), custody, an owner portal and a public case page, plus case work through month 12: outreach that brings rescuers' cases in, the operator's own rescues, intake, owner searches, ownership checks and returns. That covers known owners (a protocol, company or token holders), paid back within weeks, and unknown owners (weak or leaked keys), paid as they prove their claims.

The ideal service gives white hats legal cover when they hand funds over and pays their bounties without KYC. Where the law stops short of that, propose the design that gets closest and say where it falls short; once this RFP is funded, we pick the proposal that works and comes closest. The fee design here is a starting idea too: the team picks the legal structure, custody setup and tools, and may propose any design that solves the same problem, as long as owners pay for their rescue, the rescuer's bounty and operator's fee come only from returns, and unclaimed funds stay open to claims.
sections.out_scope:
- Rescues that need red-teaming or breaking into someone's computer or systems, this is not accecptable: rescues must start from public information, such as open-source code, onchain data or keys already published
- Tracing and freezing stolen funds
- Assets on chains other than Ethereum and its L2s
sections.who:
Nobody is pre-selected. A winning team pairs legal operations with BD and outreach people that white hats and incident-response groups already trust, since adoption pays only when rescuers hand funds over and owners are found. It needs no onchain engineering expertise.

Drafted with TheDAO Security Fund; the idea was built by Griff Green from conversations with SEAL 911, DART, TheDAO's lawyers and other teams. DART has a clear head start and may bid, as may TheDAO's lawyers.
sections.why:
This protects people whose funds sit in exploitable contracts or on leaked keys: a white hat who finds them can take them first and send them somewhere lawful. Today we leave that money on the table for the worst people in the world. White hats hold back because they want legal cover first, someone else to do the work of returning the money second, and pay third. Give them a destination they trust and they will rescue funds like mad, many just for the lulz.

- North Korea takes billions from our industry ([FBI](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226)). UN monitors found crypto theft brings in as much as half of its foreign income and helps bankroll its nuclear program ([NK News](https://www.nknews.org/2024/03/north-korea-relies-on-crypto-theft-for-up-to-half-of-foreign-income-un-report)).
- At least 220,000 people may be held in scam compounds in Myanmar and Cambodia alone, forced to run scams that include crypto fraud ([UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2023/08/1140187)).
- Anthropic measured the value AI agents could exploit from real, previously hacked contracts doubling roughly every 1.3 months ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/research/smart-contracts)). You fight AI with AI, once white hats have somewhere safe to send what they find.

initiative.summary: Our industry's security holes fund North Korea's weapons programs, scam compounds full of trafficked people, and countless cybercriminals. Black hats find exposed money and take it, while white hats who find the same holes warn the team and hope the money stays there long enough to be rescued; with AI speeding up attacks, that is a losing strategy. This RFP funds a legal entity that takes what white hats rescue, gives them legal cover, pays them without KYC, and earns its fee only when owners get their money back. Our goal is an army of white hats rescuing money everywhere they can, in effect an open bug bounty on all of Ethereum.
initiative.title: RFP: An Open Bug Bounty Program for All of Ethereum: White Hat Rescued Funds Distribution Service
